rationale: Three sensors in different rooms dropped simultaneously while the base station remains online with uplink OK, and the base station log shows E-610 "radio module self-test warning." The KB fault-code reference and historical case H-05 both indicate E-610 with multiple simultaneous peripheral drops indicates a base-station radio module fault requiring FAE escalation. The customer's Wi-Fi router theory is not applicable since these sensors communicate over sub-GHz radio to the base station, not Wi-Fi.

output.symptom_summary: Three sensors (Back Door, Living Motion, Bedroom Window) went offline simultaneously while the base station remained online with uplink OK. The base station log shows E-610 'radio module self-test warning'.
output.suspected_root_cause: Base station sub-GHz radio module fault, as indicated by E-610 and multiple simultaneous peripheral drops.

results.text: Three sensors in different rooms went offline at the same minute; base station online, RSSI history normal, E-610 in log. Restarting did not help. Escalated; radio module replaced. Escalated correctly.
Logged by the base station when its sub-GHz radio fails self-test or multiple peripherals drop simultaneously. Always escalate to FAE.
All devices offline, base station LED solid red. Router had been replaced the previous day and the Ethernet cable was in the wrong port. Resolved at frontline.

complaint: Several devices dropped at once although the base station is still online. Around breakfast the app showed the garden door sensor, the living room motion sensor and the bedroom window sensor as offline. I moved the Wi-Fi router about 2 m last week, so I assume the new position is causing interference. Everything else is working.
